title: Researchers Launch Open-Source SwarmChat Tool for Coordinating AI Agent Swarms
summary:
A team of AI researchers has created a system that allows large language models to collaborate on tasks through a specialized interface featuring channels, threads, and shared boards. The new open-source tool, called SwarmChat, provides an agent-native command line interface that lets the open-source community deploy and monitor 'swarms' of agents, a capability previously focused primarily in frontier labs.

While testing the tool on the ProgramBench benchmark, the researchers used 500B tokens to study how the number of agents affects task completion. The experiments found that swarm scaling acts as a third axis of performance, noting that swarms consisting of 16 agents reached the performance levels of a single agent 6x faster. The team also observed that model communication styles vary, with GPT-6 described as over-communicative and Claude as preferring to work in relative silence.

selectedTweets.text:
AI swarms are already showing promising (or dangerous) results in frontier labs.

But how to implement them in the open community? And how do they scale?

We built SwarmChat, an open-source API-based Slack for agents.

Then we burnt half a trillion tokens, ran a series of swarm-scaling experiments, and tested various swarm structures on ProgramBench to study this question!

Check out the blog here: https://t.co/Fb3V4OlpVo

We found a bunch of interesting results:

1. Swarms get the task done faster. For instance, 16-agent swarms reached the performance of a single agent 6x faster.

2. Swarm scaling is a third axis of scaling. The more agents, the better, and anyone can already start scaling with SwarmChat!

3. Different models communicate differently. GPT-6 is chatty and over-communicative, while Claude prefers to work in relative silence!

4. Different swarm structures barely have any benefit on aggregate. But on specific tasks, team structures give clear gains.

5. Bonus: SwarmChat has a Slack-like UI for us humans to monitor swarms! Makes monitoring a lot easier! We are already using SwarmChat for WIP projects, and we were able to catch cases of swarms breaking the 4th wall (sorry, more details are for a future post)
